aiPolicyMode.description: AI policy gate override for workspaces this rule creates: `default`, `enabled`, or `disabled`. `disabled` opts out of an *advisory* verdict only -- a **mandatory** gate ignores it, so a rule cannot carve a repository out of a fleet-wide blocking control.

aiSummaryContext.description: Free-text context given to the AI plan summariser for workspaces this rule creates (max 4000 characters).

aiSummaryMode.description: AI plan-summary opt-in for workspaces this rule creates: `default` (follow the deployment setting), `enabled`, or `disabled`.

allowForkPrPlans.description: Give fork pull requests a speculative plan on workspaces this rule creates. Defaults to false: such a plan runs the pull request author's code with the workspace's full credential set, and a fork author cannot merge, so it is the only path by which their code reaches those credentials (GHSA-gp5w-76rw-c452). Pull requests opened from branches within the repository itself are unaffected and always plan.

ansibleCollections.description: The Ansible collections a workspace created by this rule declares. Installed after the configuration's own `requirements.yml` and with `--force`, so an entry here overrides the repository's build of that collection. A fleet standardising on an internal collection is the case this exists for.

ansibleExecutionEnvironment.description: Template for a materialised workspace's operator-supplied execution environment, by label. Overrides `ansibleVersion` on the workspaces this rule creates. Available labels come from the `terrapod.getAnsibleExecutionEnvironments` data source. Leave unset and materialised workspaces run the built-in image for their line.

ansibleVersion.description: The ansible-core LINE whose execution environment this workspace's configure operations run in — `2.21`, say. Terrapod publishes one execution-environment image per line, and the line is what decides which Python versions a managed host may have, so it is the unit to pin. An exact patch (`2.21.5`) is accepted and names its own line. No HCL constraint operators and not `latest`. Left unset the server supplies the platform's current line at creation, which is then the workspace's own value — changing the platform default moves only workspaces created afterwards, exactly as `engineVersion` behaves. This does not affect how Terrapod reads the workspace's inventory: that is done server-side with the ansible in the API image.

autoApply.description: Default auto-apply setting for created workspaces. Superseded by `autoApplyMode` when that is set.

autoApplyMode.description: Conditional auto-apply mode templated onto created workspaces: `never`, `always`, `create` (apply only plans that add resources) or `createUpdate` (also allow in-place updates). Supersedes `autoApply` when set. Optional + Computed with no default so a rule that does not set it never drifts.

autoConfigureEnabled.description: Whether workspaces this rule creates queue a configure when a push changes their ansible config root. **Defaults to false.** Templated here so a fleet of configure-capable workspaces can be materialised with their trigger already on, rather than switched on one at a time.

autoMerge.description: Merge the PR automatically after a successful apply, on workspaces this rule creates.

autoMergeStrategy.description: How an auto-merge merges on workspaces this rule creates: `merge` (default), `squash` or `rebase`.

branch.description: Branch the rule scopes to. Empty (default) tracks the repo's default branch.

configDirectory.description: Repository-root-relative directory the ansible configure operation runs in on workspaces this rule creates: its fetch scope and the working directory the inventory resolver and the playbook executor both run from. **Defaults to the empty string, which is the configuration version's root**, exactly as an empty `workingDirectory` means. It does not decide whether those workspaces have a configure operation; `configureEnabled` does.

configureAfterApply.description: Whether an apply on a workspace this rule creates is followed by a configure on the same run. **Defaults to false.** A destroy apply never chains one.

configureAllHosts.description: Whether derived configures on the workspaces this rule creates target **every** host rather than only the hosts an inventory change affected. **Defaults to false**, which narrows.

configureEnabled.description: Whether workspaces this rule creates have the ansible configure operation. **Defaults to false** — configure is opt-in, so an existing rule gains no operation by upgrading. This is what declares the operation on the workspaces it creates, not the presence of a `configDirectory`. **A materialised workspace with both this and `planApplyEnabled` false is refused (422).**

debugMode.description: Hold failed runner pods open for inspection on workspaces this rule creates.

defaultLimit.description: The default `--limit` for a configure run on workspaces this rule creates, overridable per run. **Defaults to empty**, which is the whole inventory and ansible's own default. It narrows which hosts a run touches and is the configure operation's equivalent of `-target` on a terraform plan.

defaultPlaybook.description: The playbook a configure run executes on workspaces this rule creates, unless the run names another — the way `vcsRef` overrides `vcsBranch` on a run. Relative to `configDirectory`. **Defaults to empty**, meaning those workspaces declare no default and every configure run must name its playbook.

driftDetectionEnabled.description: Run scheduled drift checks on workspaces this rule creates. Defaults true, as every autodiscovered workspace is VCS-connected.

driftDetectionIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between drift checks on workspaces this rule creates. Clamped to the deployment minimum.

driftIgnoreRules.description: Resource-address/attribute-path patterns whose drift is ignored on workspaces this rule creates.

eeResourceCpu.description: CPU request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '500m'), the container a configure's playbooks run in. Separate from `resourceCpu`, which sizes the orchestrator, because the two do different work: one runs tofu, the other runs ansible against however many hosts the inventory resolves to. The limit is 2x the request. Leave unset to take the deployment default.

eeResourceMemory.description: Memory request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '1Gi'). Limit is 2x. See `eeResourceCpu`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is active. Defaults to true.

engineVersion.description: Default engine version for created workspaces — OpenTofu or Terraform, or Pulumi. Unset, the server's default ("1.12") applies.

executionBackend.description: Default execution backend for created workspaces ("tofu" or "terraform"). Defaults to "tofu".

executionHookTemplates.description: Execution hook ids (hook-<uuid>) associated with every workspace this rule creates.

executionMode.description: Default execution mode for created workspaces ("agent" or "local"). Defaults to "agent".

ignorePatterns.description: Globs filtered out before pattern matching.

inventoryPaths.description: Inventory sources templated onto workspaces this rule creates, each a file or a directory relative to the repository root. **Ordered — the order is the precedence ansible applies**, so this is a list and not a set. Name the files or directories you mean rather than a parent: `-i` over a directory holding both `production` and `staging` merges them into one inventory. Defaults to empty. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched; set `inventoryPaths = []` to clear it.

labels.description: Labels inherited by created workspaces — feeds Terrapod's label-based RBAC and filtering.

name.description: Display name for the rule. Unique per VCS connection.

nameTemplate.description: Optional template for derived workspace names. Use {path} for the dashed workingDirectory or {root} to keep slashes. Defaults to {path}.

notificationTemplates.description: Notification configurations auto-applied to workspaces created by this rule.

oidcAudiences.description: Per-provider-configuration audiences templated onto workspaces this rule creates (#1901), and their cloud identity override. A key is the provider configuration the token is for, exactly as written in a `provider` block — `aws`, `vault`, or `aws.west` for one aliased configuration; the alias is part of the key, not a nested structure. The value is always a list, even for a single audience, because several mean "these are interchangeable for this target" and some targets refuse a multi-valued `aud`. Each audience is an opaque string the federation target itself names; nothing here is specific to any one cloud. Unset (the default) means those workspaces take the deployment's audience catalogue alone. Changing it affects workspaces the rule creates from now on, not ones it has already created.

onDirectoryDelete.description: What to do with a discovered workspace when its source directory is deleted from the repository. "flag" (default, safe) marks the workspace and leaves infrastructure intact; "destroy" (opt-in) tears down the infrastructure then archives the workspace. Only "flag" or "destroy" are accepted; the server rejects other values with HTTP 422.

ownerEmail.description: Email used as ownerEmail on created workspaces. Empty = no owner; label-RBAC alone determines access.

parallelism.description: How many operations the engine performs at once on workspaces this rule creates. Defaults to 10.

pattern.description: Glob matched against changed file paths (gitignore-style with ** support).

planApplyEnabled.description: Whether workspaces this rule creates have the plan/apply operation. **Defaults to true**, so a rule that says nothing about operations goes on producing ordinary plan/apply workspaces. Set it false alongside `configureEnabled = true` for a rule that materialises configure-only workspaces. **A materialised workspace with both booleans false is refused (422)** — it could never produce a run — so do not set both false here.

planExpirySeconds.description: Seconds a plan stays applicable on workspaces this rule creates. Unset means no expiry.

resourceCpu.description: Default CPU request for runner Jobs in created workspaces. Defaults to "1".

resourceMemory.description: Default memory request for runner Jobs in created workspaces. Defaults to "2Gi".

runTaskTemplates.description: Run task definitions auto-applied to workspaces created by this rule.

securityScanEnforcement.description: IaC security-scan enforcement for workspaces this rule creates: `off` (skip), `advisory` (scan, never block — the default), or `enforced` (a failed/errored scan blocks apply until fixed or overridden).

securityScanEngine.description: Which scanner(s) run on workspaces this rule creates: `checkov` (default), `trivy`, or `both`.

securityScanSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest severity that counts as a finding on workspaces this rule creates: `critical`, `high` (default), `medium`, or `low`.

securityScanSkipRules.description: Scanner rule ids (Checkov `CKV_*` / Trivy `AVD-*`) to ignore on workspaces this rule creates.

slackChannel.description: Slack channel for run notifications on workspaces this rule creates. Empty means silent.

terraformVersion.description: Default terraform/tofu version for created workspaces. Superseded by `engineVersion`, which is the same version named for the fact that a workspace may run an engine other than Terraform.
terraformVersion.deprecationMessage: Use `engineVersion` instead. `terraformVersion` continues to work and the API will accept it indefinitely, since the terraform CLI tooling sends that name; only the provider attribute is deprecated.

terragruntEnabled.description: Run Terragrunt on workspaces this rule creates.

terragruntVersion.description: Terragrunt version for workspaces this rule creates.

varFiles.description: List of .tfvars file paths inherited by created workspaces as -var-file arguments.

vcsWorkflow.description: VCS workflow for workspaces this rule creates: `mergeThenApply` (default) or `applyThenMerge`.

agentPoolId.description: Default agent pool ID for created workspaces (e.g. "apool-abc123"). Optional.

applyOnly.description: Withhold this variable from a plan, delivering it to an apply AND to an Ansible configure. A plan executes the configuration's code, so a credential a plan does not need should not be in its environment; a configure runs the repository's playbooks against real hosts, so it is a write with apply-equivalent blast radius and receives these rows deliberately. To withhold a variable from an apply as well, use `configureOnly`. For a different value per phase, declare TWO variables with the same `key` — one ordinary and one `applyOnly` — and the apply-only one wins on an apply.

category.description: Category: terraform (or its equivalent name native), env, git_http_auth, git_ssh_auth, ansibleMachineAuth or ansible_vault_auth. `terraform` is the engine's own parameter channel -- Terraform input variables, Pulumi stack config, Ansible extra vars. One role, delivered by whichever engine the workspace runs. `native` is accepted as an equivalent name for it and does not drift -- Terrapod's own API uses that spelling, the compatibility surface this provider reads uses `terraform`, and they are one category. On a Pulumi workspace `sensitive` makes a real Pulumi secret and `structured` sets a nested config value rather than a literal dotted key. The four credential categories carry a JSON envelope rather than a literal and are ALWAYS sensitive, whatever `sensitive` says -- the provider plans it true for them so the apply does not contradict the plan. None of them accepts `valueSource = "vault"`: an envelope is an object and an OpenBao/Vault reference resolves to a single field. In the two `ansible_*` categories `key` is the credential's NAME. For `ansibleMachineAuth` the INVENTORY says where it is used, with a `${terrapod:.}` placeholder the runner substitutes while rendering -- so it can fill any connection variable, including `ansibleSshCommonArgs`, and nothing here decides placement. For `ansibleVaultAuth` the name is also the vault ID label, so several of them become one identity list and multiple vault IDs work. See the Ansible credentials documentation for each envelope's fields.

configureOnly.description: Withhold this variable from a plan AND from an apply, delivering it only to an Ansible configure. The fleet's own credential — an SSH private key to the estate, a become password — which nothing in a plan or an apply has any business holding. This is a THIRD slot rather than a variant of `applyOnly`, because a configure already receives every apply-only row: `applyOnly` means "apply and configure", so it cannot express "not in an apply either". Setting both flags on one variable is refused by the server with a 422 rather than resolved.

sensitive.description: Mark as sensitive (value will not be returned by API).

structured.description: Whether the value is a typed expression rather than a plain string. For a terraform variable that means a raw HCL expression — a list, object, number or bool rather than a quoted string.

value.description: Variable value. Sensitive variables are write-only.

valueSource.description: Where the value comes from: `static` (the default — `value` is the literal) or `vault`, where `value` holds a JSON reference (`{"mount":…,"path":…,"field":…}`) that Terrapod resolves from OpenBao (or HashiCorp Vault) at run time. A vault-sourced variable is always sensitive, and the secret is never stored in Terrapod. Add a `file` object to the reference (`"file":{"name":"gcp/adc.json"}`) to deliver the secret as a file on the runner: the variable then holds the file's absolute path, usable as `file(var.x)` or by a tool that reads a path from an environment variable. `name` defaults to the variable key; a relative name lands under `/var/run/terrapod/files/`, and a name starting with `~/` lands in the runner's home directory (e.g. `~/.aws/credentials`). Not allowed with `structured` (or its alias `hcl`). The file holds exactly one of: the reference's `field` (with `"encoding":"base64"` in `file` to decode it); a `file.template` over the whole secret, with no `field` (logic-less `{{ name | filter }}`, filters `json`, `base64decode`, `trim`, `lines`, `indent N`, and `_lease.ttl` / `_lease.renewable` / `_lease.expires_at`), to build e.g. an AWS credentials file or a PEM bundle from one read; or a `file.format` of `json` or `env` for the whole secret, optionally narrowed by `file.fields`. `{{ }}` is not Terraform interpolation, so a template needs no escaping in `jsonencode`.

valueSource.description: Where the value comes from: `static` (the default — `value` is the literal) or `vault`, where `value` holds a JSON reference (`{"mount":…,"path":…,"field":…}`) that Terrapod resolves from OpenBao (or HashiCorp Vault) at run time — so an OpenBao/Vault-backed credential can be defined once in a variable set and applied to many workspaces. A vault-sourced variable is always sensitive, and the secret is never stored in Terrapod. Add a `file` object to the reference (`"file":{"name":"gcp/adc.json"}`) to deliver the secret as a file on the runner: the variable then holds the file's absolute path. `name` defaults to the variable key; a relative name lands under `/var/run/terrapod/files/`, and a name starting with `~/` lands in the runner's home directory. Not allowed with `structured` (or its alias `hcl`). The file holds exactly one of: the reference's `field` (with `"encoding":"base64"` in `file` to decode it); a `file.template` over the whole secret, with no `field` (logic-less `{{ name | filter }}`, filters `json`, `base64decode`, `trim`, `lines`, `indent N`, and `_lease.ttl` / `_lease.renewable` / `_lease.expires_at`); or a `file.format` of `json` or `env` for the whole secret, optionally narrowed by `file.fields`. `{{ }}` is not Terraform interpolation, so a template needs no escaping in `jsonencode`.

applyOnly.description: Withhold this variable from a plan, delivering it to an apply AND to an Ansible configure, which runs the repository's playbooks against real hosts and so receives these rows deliberately. To withhold it from an apply as well, use `configureOnly`. An apply-only row shadows its standard twin inside this set's own precedence tier only — a priority set's standard row still beats a workspace apply-only one.

category.description: Category: terraform (or its equivalent name native), env, git_http_auth, git_ssh_auth, ansibleMachineAuth or ansible_vault_auth. `terraform` is the engine's own parameter channel -- Terraform input variables, Pulumi stack config, Ansible extra vars. One role, delivered by whichever engine the workspace runs. `native` is accepted as an equivalent name for it and does not drift -- Terrapod's own API uses that spelling, the compatibility surface this provider reads uses `terraform`, and they are one category. On a Pulumi workspace `sensitive` makes a real Pulumi secret and `structured` sets a nested config value rather than a literal dotted key. The four credential categories carry a JSON envelope rather than a literal and are ALWAYS sensitive, whatever `sensitive` says -- the provider plans it true for them so the apply does not contradict the plan. None of them accepts `valueSource = "vault"`: an envelope is an object and an OpenBao/Vault reference resolves to a single field. In the two `ansible_*` categories `key` is the credential's NAME. For `ansibleMachineAuth` the INVENTORY says where it is used, with a `${terrapod:.}` placeholder the runner substitutes while rendering -- so it can fill any connection variable, including `ansibleSshCommonArgs`, and nothing here decides placement. For `ansibleVaultAuth` the name is also the vault ID label, so several of them become one identity list and multiple vault IDs work. See the Ansible credentials documentation for each envelope's fields.

agentPoolId.description: Agent pool ID for agent execution mode. Assigns exactly one pool, replacing any existing set — use `agentPoolIds` to assign several. Reads back as element 0 of the set. Conflicts with `agentPoolIds`.

agentPoolIds.description: Agent pools this workspace's runs may execute on (#1085). The set is flat: a queued run is offered to every pool at once and whichever pool has a live listener claims it first, so losing one pool does not stop the workspace. There is no primary and no ordering preference. `agentPoolId` reads back as element 0. Conflicts with `agentPoolId`. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `agentPoolIds = []` to clear.

agentPoolName.description: Human-readable name of the assigned agent pool, server-derived from `agentPoolId`. Only changes when `agentPoolId` changes.

agentPoolNames.description: Read-only. The pools' names, positionally matching `agentPoolIds` — served so a consumer can render a pool without fetching the whole pool list just to turn ids into labels.

aiPolicyMode.description: Per-workspace override for the AI policy gate (#1766). One of "default", "enabled", or "disabled". Note the asymmetry: "disabled" opts out of an *advisory* verdict only — a **mandatory** gate ignores it, because a fleet-wide blocking control any workspace admin could switch off would not be a control. Defaults to "default".

aiSummaryContext.description: Workspace-specific facts appended to the AI summariser's prompt (#401). Additive to the deployment-wide fleet context. Use to flag blast-radius concerns or domain knowledge the model should weigh when describing changes for this workspace. Max 4000 characters.

aiSummaryMode.description: Per-workspace AI plan-summary opt-in (#401). One of "default" (follow the deployment's global `ai_summary.enabled` setting), "enabled" (always summarise this workspace's plans), or "disabled" (never summarise — overrides global). Defaults to "default".

allowForkPrPlans.description: Give a pull request opened from a fork a speculative plan. Defaults to false: that plan runs the pull request author's code against this workspace's whole credential set — env variables, secret-manager-resolved values, minted git credentials and the runner Job's cloud workload identity — and a fork author cannot merge, so it is the only path by which their code ever reaches those credentials (GHSA-gp5w-76rw-c452). Pull requests opened from branches within the repository itself are unaffected and always plan; turn this on only for a workspace holding nothing worth taking, such as one backing a public module repository.

ansibleCollections.description: Ansible collections installed before a configure runs. Installed AFTER the configuration's own `requirements.yml` and with `--force`, so an entry here overrides the repository's build of that collection and leaves every other one standing. Omitting the attribute leaves the stored value untouched — it does not clear it; set `ansibleCollections = []` to clear.

ansibleExecutionEnvironment.description: One of the deployment's OWN execution environments, by label — `rhel8-hardened`, say. Overrides `ansibleVersion` outright, so a workspace carrying this ignores its line entirely. A label rather than an image reference, so a workspace cannot name an arbitrary image and so the whole estate can be re-pointed in one place. Available labels come from the `terrapod.getAnsibleExecutionEnvironments` data source; naming one the deployment has not configured is refused at apply with a 422. Leave unset to run the built-in image for `ansibleVersion`, which is the ordinary case.

ansibleVersion.description: The ansible-core LINE whose execution environment this workspace's configure operations run in — `2.21`, say. Terrapod publishes one execution-environment image per line, and the line is what decides which Python versions a managed host may have, so it is the unit to pin. An exact patch (`2.21.5`) is accepted and names its own line. No HCL constraint operators and not `latest`. Left unset the server supplies the platform's current line at creation, which is then the workspace's own value — changing the platform default moves only workspaces created afterwards, exactly as `engineVersion` behaves. This does not affect how Terrapod reads the workspace's inventory: that is done server-side with the ansible in the API image.

autoApply.description: Automatically apply successful plans. Superseded by `autoApplyMode` when that is set; prefer `autoApplyMode` for new configurations.

autoApplyMode.description: Conditional auto-apply: `never`, `always`, `create` (apply only plans that add resources) or `createUpdate` (also allow in-place updates). `create` and `createUpdate` never apply a plan that destroys or replaces a resource — that is left for a human. Optional + Computed with no default, so a configuration that does not set it inherits whatever the workspace has and never drifts.

autoConfigureEnabled.description: Whether a push that changes this workspace's ansible config root queues a configure. **Defaults to false.** The run uses `defaultPlaybook` and `defaultLimit`, because a push carries no run options — which is also what bounds it: a workspace whose `defaultLimit` names a canary group cannot be made to fire wider by a git push. Needs `configureEnabled`; without it the setting is inert.

autoMerge.description: If true, Terrapod merges the PR/MR after a successful apply (subject to branch protection). Default: false.

autoMergeStrategy.description: Merge strategy for auto-merge: `merge` (default), `squash`, or `rebase`.

configDirectory.description: Repository-root-relative directory the ansible configure operation runs in: its fetch scope and the working directory the inventory resolver and the playbook executor both run from. **Defaults to the empty string, which is the configuration version's root** — exactly what an empty `workingDirectory` means. It does not decide whether the workspace *has* a configure operation; `configureEnabled` does (#1966). Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched rather than resetting it to the root; set `configDirectory = ""` to move it back to the top of the repository.

configureAfterApply.description: Whether an apply on this workspace is followed by a configure **on the same run**. **Defaults to false.** It is a workspace setting rather than a per-run option because the `terraform`/`tofu` CLI cannot pass one, and keeping the configure attached to the run is what lets a remote execution keep streaming through it. The hosts still come from the inventory and the limit from `defaultLimit` — the apply decides only *when*. A **destroy** apply never chains a configure.

configureAllHosts.description: Whether a **derived** configure — one an inventory change or an apply produced, rather than one somebody asked for with a limit — targets **every** host rather than only the hosts that changed. **Defaults to false**, which narrows. Narrowing is conditioned on what justifies breadth: new playbook or role code has to reach every host, while a changed *host* is no reason to touch the others. So a derived configure narrows when the ansible code under `configDirectory` is unchanged since the last successful configure, and goes wide when it moved. This flag is the override and it **widens** — a flag someone forgets leaves them configuring more, not less.

configureEnabled.description: Whether this workspace has the ansible configure operation. **Defaults to false**, so configure is opt-in and no existing workspace gains an operation by upgrading. This is what declares the operation — not the presence of a `configDirectory`, which is now an ordinary path whose empty value means the configuration version's root. **A workspace with both `configureEnabled` and `planApplyEnabled` false is refused (422).**

debugMode.description: Hold this workspace's failed runner pods open so they can be exec'd into. A failed run's container is normally terminated immediately, which is exactly when you want to look inside it. How long a pod lingers is the deployment's `runners.debugLingerSeconds`, not this resource's — the pod keeps the run's credentials for that window.

defaultLimit.description: The default `--limit` for a configure run, overridable per run. Empty means the whole inventory, which is ansible's own default. This narrows which hosts a run touches and is the configure operation's equivalent of `-target` on a terraform plan.

defaultPlaybook.description: The playbook a configure run executes unless the run names another, the way `vcsRef` overrides `vcsBranch` on a run. Relative to `configDirectory`. Empty means the workspace has no default and every configure run must name its playbook.

driftDetectionEnabled.description: Enable drift detection for this workspace. Defaults to true for VCS-connected workspaces, false otherwise.

driftDetectionIntervalSeconds.description: Interval in seconds between drift detection checks.

driftIgnoreRules.description: Glob-aware patterns suppressed by the drift-result classifier (#482). Each entry is a Terraform resource address optionally suffixed with a dotted attribute path; `*` matches zero or more non-`.` characters (so it can span `[N]` indices but not segment boundaries), and `[*]` matches any bracketed index. A bare address with no attribute suffix silences any change to that resource — including destroys — so use carefully. Examples: `aws_iam_role.foo.tags.Environment`, `aws_autoscaling_group.workers[*].desired_capacity`, `module.eks*.argocd_cluster.*.config.tls_client_config.ca_data`, `aws_iam_role.foo`. Empty list (the default) means classic drift behaviour: every plan diff counts. Affects drift-detection runs only — regular plan/apply is untouched. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `driftIgnoreRules = []` to clear.

driftLastCheckedAt.description: Timestamp of the last drift check. Server-volatile.

driftLatestRunId.description: ID of the drift run that produced the current `driftStatus`, prefixed `run-…`. Empty when drift has never run or when cleared by a successful apply. Server-volatile.

driftStatus.description: Current drift status: "" (never checked), "noDrift", "drifted", or "errored". Server-volatile — updates when a drift run completes.

eeResourceCpu.description: CPU request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '500m'), the container a configure's playbooks run in. Separate from `resourceCpu`, which sizes the orchestrator, because the two do different work: one runs tofu, the other runs ansible against however many hosts the inventory resolves to. The limit is 2x the request. Leave unset to take the deployment default.

eeResourceMemory.description: Memory request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '1Gi'). Limit is 2x. See `eeResourceCpu`.

engine.description: The execution engine family this workspace belongs to ("terraform" by default, or another engine the deployment enables). Distinct from execution_backend, which picks the binary within the Terraform engine. Changing it replaces the workspace.

engineVersion.description: The version of the engine this workspace runs — OpenTofu or Terraform, or Pulumi. A partial version like `1.12` means the latest `1.12.*`; no HCL constraint operators.

executionBackend.description: Which binary runs a Terraform-engine workspace: `terraform` or `tofu`. Defaults to `terraform`. This is a choice WITHIN the Terraform engine — Pulumi has one binary, so the attribute has no meaning on a `pulumi` workspace and is left to the server there rather than defaulted.

inventoryPaths.description: Inventory sources, each a file or a directory relative to the repository root. **Ordered — the order is the precedence ansible applies**, so this is a list and not a set. Name the files or directories you mean rather than a parent: `-i` over a directory containing both `production` and `staging` merges them into one inventory. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `inventoryPaths = []` to clear.

labels.description: Labels for RBAC evaluation (key-value pairs).

lifecycleReason.description: Human-readable explanation of `lifecycleState`. Empty for active workspaces. Server-volatile.

lifecycleState.description: Autodiscovery lifecycle state for managed workspaces: "active", "pendingDeletion", or "archived". Server-volatile — autodiscovery lifecycle reconciler can move this between plan and apply.

lockReason.description: Why the workspace is locked, as given when the lock was taken. Null when unlocked or when no reason was given. Server-volatile.

locked.description: Whether the workspace is locked. Server-volatile — operators can lock/unlock via the API outside of Terraform.

lockedBy.description: Identity that took the workspace lock. Null when unlocked. Server-volatile.

name.description: The workspace name.

oidcAudiences.description: Per-provider-configuration audiences a run's identity token is minted for, and this workspace's cloud identity override (#1901). A key is the provider configuration the token is for, exactly as written in a `provider` block — `aws`, `vault`, or `aws.west` for one aliased configuration; the alias is part of the key, not a nested structure. The value is always a list, even for a single audience: a list of several is a deliberate "these are interchangeable for this target" statement, and some targets refuse a multi-valued `aud` outright. Each audience is an opaque string the federation target itself names — whatever your cloud's or secret store's trust configuration expects — and Terrapod stores it verbatim; nothing here is specific to any one cloud. Terrapod mints one OIDC JWT per key and the runner writes it to a file; which provider reads that file, and what it does with it, is your own provider configuration. This attribute is an OVERRIDE over the deployment's own audience catalogue, so it holds only the keys you set here — a key the deployment supplies and this configuration does not is used by the workspace but is deliberately not recorded in state, exactly as the AWS provider's `tags` does not absorb `defaultTags`. Read the effective merged set from the `terrapod.Workspace` data source. Say "no audiences for this target" by REMOVING the key, which falls back to the deployment value; an empty list under a key is refused. At most 10 keys, 10 audiences each, 255 characters per audience. A token audienced for two targets is replayable between them, so name only the targets this workspace federates to. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `oidcAudiences = {}` to clear every override, which falls the workspace back to the deployment catalogue alone.

parallelism.description: How many operations the engine performs at once (-parallelism for terraform/tofu). Defaults to 10, terraform's own default. Raise it for a large state on a well-resourced runner; lower it to stay inside a provider's rate limit.

planApplyEnabled.description: Whether this workspace has the plan/apply operation — the terraform, OpenTofu or Pulumi half. **Defaults to true**, so a workspace that says nothing about its operations behaves exactly as every workspace did before this attribute existed. Setting it false makes the workspace configure-only. **A workspace with both `planApplyEnabled` and `configureEnabled` false is refused (422)**: it could never produce a run, and `locked` is the reversible way to park a workspace.

planExpirySeconds.description: Per-workspace plan expiry TTL in seconds (#646). An apply-capable planned run older than this is auto-discarded and must be re-planned. Unset / 0 = disabled (the default).

pulumiBindPlan.description: Pulumi workspaces only: bind the update to the approved preview (`preview --save-plan` then `up --plan`). Off by default, which runs a plain `pulumi up`. Rests on Pulumi update plans, still experimental upstream. Setting it true on any other engine is rejected.

remoteStateConsumers.description: Workspace IDs authorized to read this workspace's state via `terraformRemoteState` (#344). Optional + Computed: leave null to opt out of managing the set here (server side is left intact — useful when consumers are managed via standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources elsewhere). Set to `[]` to explicitly remove all consumers. **Do not mix this attribute with standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources targeting the same producer** — the two will drift on every plan and fight each other. Mutations require admin/write on this (producer) workspace; a consumer team cannot self-grant.

resourceCpu.description: CPU request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '1').

resourceMemory.description: Memory request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '2Gi').

securityScanEnforcement.description: IaC security-scan enforcement: `off` (skip), `advisory` (scan, never block — the default), or `enforced` (a failed/errored scan blocks apply until fixed or overridden).

securityScanEngine.description: Which scanner(s) run: `checkov` (default), `trivy`, or `both` (union of findings, deduped).

securityScanSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest finding severity that counts as a failure: `critical`, `high` (default), `medium`, or `low`.

securityScanSkipRules.description: Scanner rule-ids to suppress (Checkov `CKV_*` / Trivy `AVD-*`). Empty list (default) skips nothing. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `securityScanSkipRules = []` to clear.

slackChannel.description: Slack channel this workspace's run notifications post to (#556) — approval / applied / errored / drift. Opt-in: leave empty and the workspace stays silent (there is no deployment-wide fan-out). Requires the Slack app to be enabled server-side.

stateDiverged.description: True when an apply Job succeeded but uploading the resulting state to Terrapod failed; the recorded state is out of sync with reality. Stable across PATCHes — only the state-upload pathway changes this.

terraformVersion.description: The Terraform/OpenTofu version to use. Superseded by `engineVersion`, which is the same version named for the fact that a workspace may run an engine other than Terraform.
terraformVersion.deprecationMessage: Use `engineVersion` instead. `terraformVersion` continues to work and the API will accept it indefinitely, since the terraform CLI tooling sends that name; only the provider attribute is deprecated.

terragruntEnabled.description: Wrap tofu/terraform with terragrunt for agent-mode runs. See https://terrapod.dev for the agent-mode limitations.

terragruntVersion.description: The terragrunt CLI version to use when terragruntEnabled is true. Partial versions (e.g. "1.0") are resolved by the binary cache. Defaults to "1.0".

triggerPrefixes.description: Repo-root-relative directories to include in the sparse VCS fetch in addition to `workingDirectory`. Required when the workspace's terraform crosses directory boundaries via relative module sources (`module "foo" { source = "../foo" }`) — sparse-checkout cone mode includes parents of the listed directories but NOT siblings, so the referenced sibling must be declared here or the runner will error with `Unable to evaluate directory symlink`. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `triggerPrefixes = []` to clear.

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp. Server-volatile — ticks on every PATCH and on every server-side write (drift detection, VCS poll, lifecycle reconciler).

varFiles.description: List of .tfvars file paths passed as -var-file arguments to plan/apply. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `varFiles = []` to clear.

vcsConnectionName.description: Human-readable name of the assigned VCS connection, server-derived from `vcsConnectionId`. Only changes when `vcsConnectionId` changes.

vcsLastAttemptedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent VCS poll attempt, successful or not. `vcsLastPolledAt` only advances on success, so a gap between the two identifies a workspace whose polls are failing. Server-volatile.

vcsLastError.description: Most recent VCS poll error message. Empty when the last poll succeeded. Server-volatile.

vcsLastErrorAt.description: Timestamp of `vcsLastError`. Server-volatile.

vcsLastPolledAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful VCS poll cycle. Server-volatile — VCS poller writes this every `vcs.poll_interval_seconds` (default 60s).

vcsRepoUrl.description: Git HTTPS URL for VCS integration.

vcsWorkflow.description: VCS workflow mode: `mergeThenApply` (default, TFE/HCP standard) or `applyThenMerge` (Atlantis-style; PR runs are full plan-and-apply that wait on a `terrapod apply` comment). Apply-then-merge requires a VCS connection and is incompatible with `auto_apply=true`.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory relative to the repo root.

Note the asymmetry: "disabled" opts out of an *advisory* verdict only — a **mandatory** gate ignores it, because a fleet-wide blocking control any workspace admin could switch off would not be a control. allowForkPrPlans.description: Give a pull request opened from a fork a speculative plan. ansibleCollections.description: Ansible collections installed before a configure runs. Leave unset to run the built-in image for `ansibleVersion`, which is the ordinary case.

autoApply.description: Automatically apply successful plans. Superseded by `autoApplyMode` when that is set; prefer `autoApplyMode` for new configurations.

autoApplyMode.description: Conditional auto-apply: `never`, `always`, `create` (apply only plans that add resources) or `createUpdate` (also allow in-place updates). `create` and `createUpdate` never apply a plan that destroys or replaces a resource — that is left for a human. Optional + Computed with no default, so a configuration that does not set it inherits whatever the workspace has and never drifts.

autoMerge.description: If true, Terrapod merges the PR/MR after a successful apply (subject to branch protection). Default: false.

autoMergeStrategy.description: Merge strategy for auto-merge: `merge` (default), `squash`, or `rebase`.

configDirectory.description: Repository-root-relative directory the ansible configure operation runs in: its fetch scope and the working directory the inventory resolver and the playbook executor both run from. **Defaults to the empty string, which is the configuration version's root** — exactly what an empty `workingDirectory` means. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched rather than resetting it to the root; set `configDirectory = ""` to move it back to the top of the repository.

configureAfterApply.description: Whether an apply on this workspace is followed by a configure **on the same run**. **Defaults to false.** It is a workspace setting rather than a per-run option because the `terraform`/`tofu` CLI cannot pass one, and keeping the configure attached to the run is what lets a remote execution keep streaming through it. The hosts still come from the inventory and the limit from `defaultLimit` — the apply decides only *when*. A **destroy** apply never chains a configure.

configureAllHosts.description: Whether a **derived** configure — one an inventory change or an apply produced, rather than one somebody asked for with a limit — targets **every** host rather than only the hosts that changed. **Defaults to false**, which narrows. Narrowing is conditioned on what justifies breadth: new playbook or role code has to reach every host, while a changed *host* is no reason to touch the others. So a derived configure narrows when the ansible code under `configDirectory` is unchanged since the last successful configure, and goes wide when it moved. This flag is the override and it **widens** — a flag someone forgets leaves them configuring more, not less.

configureEnabled.description: Whether this workspace has the ansible configure operation. **Defaults to false**, so configure is opt-in and no existing workspace gains an operation by upgrading. debugMode.description: Hold this workspace's failed runner pods open so they can be exec'd into. A failed run's container is normally terminated immediately, which is exactly when you want to look inside it. How long a pod lingers is the deployment's `runners.debugLingerSeconds`, not this resource's — the pod keeps the run's credentials for that window.

defaultPlaybook.description: The playbook a configure run executes unless the run names another, the way `vcsRef` overrides `vcsBranch` on a run. Relative to `configDirectory`. Empty means the workspace has no default and every configure run must name its playbook.

driftDetectionEnabled.description: Enable drift detection for this workspace. Defaults to true for VCS-connected workspaces, false otherwise.

driftDetectionIntervalSeconds.description: Interval in seconds between drift detection checks.

driftIgnoreRules.description: Glob-aware patterns suppressed by the drift-result classifier (#482). Each entry is a Terraform resource address optionally suffixed with a dotted attribute path; `*` matches zero or more non-`.` characters (so it can span `[N]` indices but not segment boundaries), and `[*]` matches any bracketed index. eeResourceCpu.description: CPU request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '500m'), the container a configure's playbooks run in. Separate from `resourceCpu`, which sizes the orchestrator, because the two do different work: one runs tofu, the other runs ansible against however many hosts the inventory resolves to. The limit is 2x the request. Leave unset to take the deployment default.

eeResourceMemory.description: Memory request for the Ansible execution-environment sidecar (K8s format, e.g. '1Gi'). Limit is 2x. See `eeResourceCpu`.

engine.description: The execution engine family this workspace belongs to ("terraform" by default, or another engine the deployment enables). Distinct from execution_backend, which picks the binary within the Terraform engine. Changing it replaces the workspace.

engineVersion.description: The version of the engine this workspace runs — OpenTofu or Terraform, or Pulumi. A partial version like `1.12` means the latest `1.12.*`; no HCL constraint operators.

executionBackend.description: Which binary runs a Terraform-engine workspace: `terraform` or `tofu`. Defaults to `terraform`. This is a choice WITHIN the Terraform engine — Pulumi has one binary, so the attribute has no meaning on a `pulumi` workspace and is left to the server there rather than defaulted.

inventoryPaths.description: Inventory sources, each a file or a directory relative to the repository root. **Ordered — the order is the precedence ansible applies**, so this is a list and not a set. Name the files or directories you mean rather than a parent: `-i` over a directory containing both `production` and `staging` merges them into one inventory. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `inventoryPaths = []` to clear.

labels.description: Labels for RBAC evaluation (key-value pairs).

name.description: The workspace name.

oidcAudiences.description: Per-provider-configuration audiences a run's identity token is minted for, and this workspace's cloud identity override (#1901). Each audience is an opaque string the federation target itself names — whatever your cloud's or secret store's trust configuration expects — and Terrapod stores it verbatim; nothing here is specific to any one cloud. Terrapod mints one OIDC JWT per key and the runner writes it to a file; which provider reads that file, and what it does with it, is your own provider configuration. This attribute is an OVERRIDE over the deployment's own audience catalogue, so it holds only the keys you set here — a key the deployment supplies and this configuration does not is used by the workspace but is deliberately not recorded in state, exactly as the AWS provider's `tags` does not absorb `defaultTags`. Read the effective merged set from the `terrapod.Workspace` data source. Say "no audiences for this target" by REMOVING the key, which falls back to the deployment value; an empty list under a key is refused. At most 10 keys, 10 audiences each, 255 characters per audience. A token audienced for two targets is replayable between them, so name only the targets this workspace federates to. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `oidcAudiences = {}` to clear every override, which falls the workspace back to the deployment catalogue alone.

parallelism.description: How many operations the engine performs at once (-parallelism for terraform/tofu). Defaults to 10, terraform's own default. Raise it for a large state on a well-resourced runner; lower it to stay inside a provider's rate limit.

planApplyEnabled.description: Whether this workspace has the plan/apply operation — the terraform, OpenTofu or Pulumi half. **Defaults to true**, so a workspace that says nothing about its operations behaves exactly as every workspace did before this attribute existed. planExpirySeconds.description: Per-workspace plan expiry TTL in seconds (#646). An apply-capable planned run older than this is auto-discarded and must be re-planned. Unset / 0 = disabled (the default).

pulumiBindPlan.description: Pulumi workspaces only: bind the update to the approved preview (`preview --save-plan` then `up --plan`). Off by default, which runs a plain `pulumi up`. Rests on Pulumi update plans, still experimental upstream. Setting it true on any other engine is rejected.

remoteStateConsumers.description: Workspace IDs authorized to read this workspace's state via `terraformRemoteState` (#344). Optional + Computed: leave null to opt out of managing the set here (server side is left intact — useful when consumers are managed via standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources elsewhere). Set to `[]` to explicitly remove all consumers. **Do not mix this attribute with standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources targeting the same producer** — the two will drift on every plan and fight each other. Mutations require admin/write on this (producer) workspace; a consumer team cannot self-grant.

resourceCpu.description: CPU request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '1').

resourceMemory.description: Memory request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '2Gi').

securityScanEnforcement.description: IaC security-scan enforcement: `off` (skip), `advisory` (scan, never block — the default), or `enforced` (a failed/errored scan blocks apply until fixed or overridden).

securityScanEngine.description: Which scanner(s) run: `checkov` (default), `trivy`, or `both` (union of findings, deduped).

securityScanSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest finding severity that counts as a failure: `critical`, `high` (default), `medium`, or `low`.

securityScanSkipRules.description: Scanner rule-ids to suppress (Checkov `CKV_*` / Trivy `AVD-*`). Empty list (default) skips nothing. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `securityScanSkipRules = []` to clear.

slackChannel.description: Slack channel this workspace's run notifications post to (#556) — approval / applied / errored / drift. Opt-in: leave empty and the workspace stays silent (there is no deployment-wide fan-out). Requires the Slack app to be enabled server-side.

terraformVersion.description: The Terraform/OpenTofu version to use. Superseded by `engineVersion`, which is the same version named for the fact that a workspace may run an engine other than Terraform.
terraformVersion.deprecationMessage: Use `engineVersion` instead. `terraformVersion` continues to work and the API will accept it indefinitely, since the terraform CLI tooling sends that name; only the provider attribute is deprecated.

terragruntEnabled.description: Wrap tofu/terraform with terragrunt for agent-mode runs. See https://terrapod.dev for the agent-mode limitations.

terragruntVersion.description: The terragrunt CLI version to use when terragruntEnabled is true. Partial versions (e.g. "1.0") are resolved by the binary cache. Defaults to "1.0".

This attribute is an OVERRIDE over the deployment's own audience catalogue, so it holds only the keys you set here — a key the deployment supplies and this configuration does not is used by the workspace but is deliberately not recorded in state, exactly as the AWS provider's `tags` does not absorb `defaultTags`. Read the effective merged set from the `terrapod.Workspace` data source. Say "no audiences for this target" by REMOVING the key, which falls back to the deployment value; an empty list under a key is refused. At most 10 keys, 10 audiences each, 255 characters per audience. A token audienced for two targets is replayable between them, so name only the targets this workspace federates to. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `oidcAudiences = {}` to clear every override, which falls the workspace back to the deployment catalogue alone.

parallelism.description: How many operations the engine performs at once (-parallelism for terraform/tofu). Defaults to 10, terraform's own default. Raise it for a large state on a well-resourced runner; lower it to stay inside a provider's rate limit.

planApplyEnabled.description: Whether this workspace has the plan/apply operation — the terraform, OpenTofu or Pulumi half. **Defaults to true**, so a workspace that says nothing about its operations behaves exactly as every workspace did before this attribute existed. Setting it false makes the workspace configure-only. **A workspace with both `planApplyEnabled` and `configureEnabled` false is refused (422)**: it could never produce a run, and `locked` is the reversible way to park a workspace.

planExpirySeconds.description: Per-workspace plan expiry TTL in seconds (#646). An apply-capable planned run older than this is auto-discarded and must be re-planned. Unset / 0 = disabled (the default).

pulumiBindPlan.description: Pulumi workspaces only: bind the update to the approved preview (`preview --save-plan` then `up --plan`). Off by default, which runs a plain `pulumi up`. Rests on Pulumi update plans, still experimental upstream. Setting it true on any other engine is rejected.

remoteStateConsumers.description: Workspace IDs authorized to read this workspace's state via `terraformRemoteState` (#344). Optional + Computed: leave null to opt out of managing the set here (server side is left intact — useful when consumers are managed via standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources elsewhere). Set to `[]` to explicitly remove all consumers. **Do not mix this attribute with standalone `terrapod.RemoteStateConsumer` resources targeting the same producer** — the two will drift on every plan and fight each other. Mutations require admin/write on this (producer) workspace; a consumer team cannot self-grant.

resourceCpu.description: CPU request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '1').

resourceMemory.description: Memory request for runner Jobs (K8s format, e.g. '2Gi').

securityScanEnforcement.description: IaC security-scan enforcement: `off` (skip), `advisory` (scan, never block — the default), or `enforced` (a failed/errored scan blocks apply until fixed or overridden).

securityScanEngine.description: Which scanner(s) run: `checkov` (default), `trivy`, or `both` (union of findings, deduped).

securityScanSeverityThreshold.description: Lowest finding severity that counts as a failure: `critical`, `high` (default), `medium`, or `low`.

securityScanSkipRules.description: Scanner rule-ids to suppress (Checkov `CKV_*` / Trivy `AVD-*`). Empty list (default) skips nothing. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `securityScanSkipRules = []` to clear.

slackChannel.description: Slack channel this workspace's run notifications post to (#556) — approval / applied / errored / drift. Opt-in: leave empty and the workspace stays silent (there is no deployment-wide fan-out). Requires the Slack app to be enabled server-side.

stateDiverged.description: True when an apply Job succeeded but uploading the resulting state to Terrapod failed; the recorded state is out of sync with reality. Stable across PATCHes — only the state-upload pathway changes this.

terraformVersion.description: The Terraform/OpenTofu version to use. Superseded by `engineVersion`, which is the same version named for the fact that a workspace may run an engine other than Terraform.
terraformVersion.deprecationMessage: Use `engineVersion` instead. `terraformVersion` continues to work and the API will accept it indefinitely, since the terraform CLI tooling sends that name; only the provider attribute is deprecated.

terragruntEnabled.description: Wrap tofu/terraform with terragrunt for agent-mode runs. See https://terrapod.dev for the agent-mode limitations.

terragruntVersion.description: The terragrunt CLI version to use when terragruntEnabled is true. Partial versions (e.g. "1.0") are resolved by the binary cache. Defaults to "1.0".

triggerPrefixes.description: Repo-root-relative directories to include in the sparse VCS fetch in addition to `workingDirectory`. Required when the workspace's terraform crosses directory boundaries via relative module sources (`module "foo" { source = "../foo" }`) — sparse-checkout cone mode includes parents of the listed directories but NOT siblings, so the referenced sibling must be declared here or the runner will error with `Unable to evaluate directory symlink`. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `triggerPrefixes = []` to clear.

updatedAt.description: Last update timestamp. Server-volatile — ticks on every PATCH and on every server-side write (drift detection, VCS poll, lifecycle reconciler).

varFiles.description: List of .tfvars file paths passed as -var-file arguments to plan/apply. Omitting this attribute leaves any existing server-side value untouched — it does not clear it; set `varFiles = []` to clear.

vcsConnectionName.description: Human-readable name of the assigned VCS connection, server-derived from `vcsConnectionId`. Only changes when `vcsConnectionId` changes.

vcsLastAttemptedAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent VCS poll attempt, successful or not. `vcsLastPolledAt` only advances on success, so a gap between the two identifies a workspace whose polls are failing. Server-volatile.

vcsLastError.description: Most recent VCS poll error message. Empty when the last poll succeeded. Server-volatile.

vcsLastErrorAt.description: Timestamp of `vcsLastError`. Server-volatile.

vcsLastPolledAt.description: Timestamp of the most recent successful VCS poll cycle. Server-volatile — VCS poller writes this every `vcs.poll_interval_seconds` (default 60s).

vcsRepoUrl.description: Git HTTPS URL for VCS integration.

vcsWorkflow.description: VCS workflow mode: `mergeThenApply` (default, TFE/HCP standard) or `applyThenMerge` (Atlantis-style; PR runs are full plan-and-apply that wait on a `terrapod apply` comment). Apply-then-merge requires a VCS connection and is incompatible with `auto_apply=true`.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory relative to the repo root.
